item.title: DELVEMAN: Artificial intelligence is funny, so it can't be that bad
item.description:
# DELVEMAN: Artificial intelligence is funny, so it can't be that bad ## I don’t know what the hell a Luddite is, but The Cavalier Daily does, and they can’t be wrong! ![In a world of uncertainty and remarkably unfunny public figures, it’s Tung or be Tunged.](https://snworksceo.imgix.net/cav/8b12de83-33ec-4425-93d2-c7fa1633c789.sized-1000x1000.png?w=1000)
Most of you are probably aware of artificial intelligence. Thus, as a member of the over-eight-hours-of-screentime club, I loathe those jaundiced, [bitter](https://www.cavalierdaily.com/article/2026/06/editorial-it-is-not-the-time-for-a-revenge-of-the-luddites?ct=content_open&cv=cbox_latest) fools who want to pop our AI bubble for good.
In a world of uncertainty and remarkably unfunny [public figures](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2025/nov/13/it-soothes-my-bitter-heart-to-know-that-no-matter-how-much-money-elon-musk-has-he-will-never-ever-be-funny), it’s Tung or be Tunged. We’re in a memetic arms race where only the silly will survive, and AI is the surest way for the [righteous](https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2026/04/16/pete-hegseth-quotes-violent-prayer-from-pulp-fiction-references-bible/) to win this new war. Without further ado, let’s [slop](https://www.merriam-webster.com/wordplay/word-of-the-year) it up.
First, allow me to direct your attention to Exhibit A — An AI-generated chatbot of Vecna from “Stranger Things” [calling](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DTOoopojXgF/) a hotel to try to book a room for Jan. 7. Only half of their reels are actually scambaiting, though, because badgering customer service [workers](https://insights.som.yale.edu/insights/the-real-job-destruction-from-ai-is-hitting-before-careers-can-start) is also pretty funny!
Anyway, [Vecna](https://www.giantfreakinrobot.com/ent/scifi/vecna-worst.html). Or AI-generated Vecna. In a vacuum, using AI to assist one's writing is perfectly [fine](https://youtube.com/shorts/ms-JPUkYbuQ?is=Xu_lIOAMJurQhyKb).
The already-artificial aesthetic of this show, when coupled with the notion that its undead wizard villain both has a credit card and wants to book a hotel room, lend themselves to creating an exceptionally funny bit of short-form content. Could an impersonator do the same thing? Probably. But what if you had like 10 impersonators and they didn’t care about things like “tact” or “empathy”?
What was formerly accomplished by slapping neon text on a dark background, a stock image or a photo of the University is now accomplished by feeding ChatGPT a sentence and waiting like 20 seconds.
Most of our readers go to college, and I’m sure you all get that. You’re not even the social chair, you don’t understand it. It’s worth the [water](https://news.mit.edu/2025/explained-generative-ai-environmental-impact-0117), dude.
“But if AI is so funny and useful and awesome, why isn’t the government using it?” you might ask. The brightest minds of the second Trump administration have used AI-generated “content” to, uh, bolster the [innovative](https://www.tiktok.com/@whitehouse/video/7647656978956799246) [message](https://www.tiktok.com/@whitehouse/video/7645123289521687821) for change spearheaded by President Donald [Trump](https://www.tiktok.com/@whitehouse/video/7640550321856498957), of course.
Even if you disagree with the White House, AI is just the fix you need. When The Cavalier Daily Editorial Board alluded to AI as “an opportunity to disrupt the status quo,” this is what they meant! Anti-Trump advocates should simply use these [neutral](https://www.chapman.edu/ai/bias-in-ai.aspx) tools to disseminate fictional videos to millions of impartial voters.
In the end, all of this evidence goes to show that AI can do it all. From the highest office in the land down to your own personal algorithm, AI makes the world a [sillier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic%E2%80%93United_States_Department_of_Defense_dispute) place. Need a [laugh](https://www.hks.harvard.edu/faculty-research/policy-topics/science-technology-data/daily-ai-use-associated-depressive-symptoms)? AI has your back! Need a [friend](https://www.media.mit.edu/articles/chatgpt-may-be-making-us-lonelier/)? AI’s right there for you. Need a job? Well … if your degree is “bound for the history books” and your dream job is “redundant,” it sounds like you’re perfectly qualified to start [training](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/aug/02/ai-chatbot-training-human-toll-content-moderator-meta-openai) a large language model!

item.title: Shore Musings: On Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
# Shore Musings: On Artificial Intelligence ## We can make things faster and cheaper now. But for the consumer, that's more like a regression. In a world of AI-generated Sonic T-shirts, thanks, TJ McGlade, for airbrushing the Sonic T-shirt of my dreams.
The claim increasingly seems like a defense mechanism, a way of taking power back from the AI Cambrian explosion touching most of Earth’s citizens.
It loses its uniqueness or flair. As far as running a business, with direct-to-garment printing, vinyl, and now with AI as a competitor in the ring, I think it becomes a lot harder for traditional artists to survive."
We can make things faster and cheaper now.
I have seen some of our peers shrink in page count, and eventually, turn to AI generation for both cover art and article content.
Because one day, you might find that your specialized ability has been automated too.
